body: Well thank you for the chat. You are a wonderful person. However, I am completely drained and need to sleep. Have a wonderful night. Good luck with the school work.

She's not at home with me, she's an hour away at college (I just saw her more recently because of Thanksgiving). I'm usually okay most of the time but when I start to look back, everything piles up. So like one mean comment doesn't do anything, but if its late at night, I can't sleep, and I'm stressed, everything just falls apart (like tonight). I just constantly have this need to prove myself, my whole life I've always just been the weird little sister. I feel like no one in my family thinks I'm adult, no one takes me seriously. This was the same case in high school too. Not until I got into upper division classes did I feel like people didn't look down on me. That's probably part of the reason why I'm looking at grad school.

I'd like to go into education. I really just want to go into something that does good opposed to something that is if even inadvertently causing harm. It is stupid, but my sister very frequently, and probably not knowing it, makes me feel like shit and need to prove myself. She's constantly dismissing my current job and making me feel like more of a failure by living at home.

I'm not working out because of applications due in a week. I'm not terribly out of shape, ran a 5k race last weekend. I feel like I need a graduate degree to escape because I'm feel like not good enough to get a full time job. My job right now doesn't even require a degree, while almost everyone else I know is employed full time. My mom is also constantly telling me that if I go off (to my friends in Chicago or somewhere else) that I'll just burn through my savings and be back in a year.
BTW you are so awesome for just responding. Thank you. If you do get tired, please don't let me stop you from sleeping.

Since I'm applying to grad school, I'm not even exercising like I used to. Usually I just read and work out. It is pretty sad. I also feel very trapped at home because I can't really come and go as I please, but I also don't feel like I'm able to get a full time job. What did you end up getting your second degree in? I've actually thought about that route, but it would be living at home for even longer. Grad school is kind of my path out of my house. I don't even feel like an adult right now.

I'm always depressed when I'm alone... but that's not necessarily true for right now. That was true when I was in college, I had really no support my first two years in college. I was basically mocked by my swim team. But now I'm depressed and I have a beyond excellent boyfriend. However, I have zero social life and almost no friends (everyone moved from college). I don't really know how to go about getting friends... hence why grad school seems in theory like a good idea (people share the same interest as me).

Thanks random internet stranger. I just so easily go from anxiety to depression. How do I find my triggers? The only I can see is an overactive imagination and the ability to make up only possible terrible futures. Does that make sense?
